accessibility_check.what: Accessibility settings like Zoom and VoiceOver
accessibility_check.why: Helpful features such as zoom, contrast and sticky keys are easy to miss or turn on by accident.
accessibility_check.where: `defaults read com.apple.universalaccess`, global trackpad and mouse settings

accessibility_permissions.what: Apps allowed to control your Mac
accessibility_permissions.why: This access lets an app click, type and read the screen, so it should only go to apps you trust.

ai_agent_audit.what: AI tools and the add-ons they can reach
ai_agent_audit.why: AI assistants can be linked to add-ons or saved keys that reach far into your files and accounts.

ai_threat_indicators.what: Programs and background tasks that use AI services
ai_threat_indicators.why: Programs talking to AI services that you didn't set up can be a sign of unwanted automation.

ai_worm_filesystem.what: Known bad files and scripts that hide what they do
ai_worm_filesystem.why: Some bad code packages leave scripts behind that fetch and run more code.
ai_worm_filesystem.where: known worm file paths and hashes; scripts in ~/.local/bin, ~/.config, ~/.cache, /tmp

ai_worm_git_ssh.what: Developer settings that can run hidden code
ai_worm_git_ssh.why: Self-spreading code packages change git, npm, AI tool and SSH settings to run code or let someone in.

ai_worm_lateral.what: Signs of stolen keys and copies spread to projects
ai_worm_lateral.why: Self-spreading code packages collect passwords and cloud keys and use them to publish copies.
ai_worm_lateral.where: known stolen-key paths, workflow files under ~/src, `lsof -i -n -P`, `npm whoami`

ai_worm_network.what: Network connections to known bad or repeating servers
ai_worm_network.why: Malware often keeps checking in with a remote server or sends saved sign-ins away.

ai_worm_persistence.what: Startup items left by self-spreading code
ai_worm_persistence.why: Malware from bad code packages often sets itself to start again after a restart.

airdrop_config.what: Who can send you files with AirDrop
airdrop_config.why: When AirDrop is open to everyone, people nearby can send you files and see your device name.
airdrop_config.where: `defaults read com.apple.sharingd DiscoverableMode`, Bluetooth and Wi-Fi power

airdrop_security_check.what: AirDrop, Handoff and nearby sharing settings
airdrop_security_check.why: Nearby sharing features can make your device visible to people around you.

airport_wifi_scan.what: Wi-Fi signal and nearby network crowding
airport_wifi_scan.why: A weak signal or a crowded channel can make Wi-Fi drop or feel slow.

antivirus_status.why: Knowing which virus protection is present and current shows how well the computer is covered.
antivirus_status.where: XProtect.bundle and MRT.app versions, antivirus apps in /Applications, `pgrep -i`

app_crash_analyzer.why: Repeated crashes can point to an app that needs updating or a memory problem.

app_permissions.what: Apps allowed to use the camera, microphone or screen
app_permissions.why: These permissions let an app see or hear what is around the computer, so trust matters.
app_permissions.where: camera, microphone and screen entries in /Library/Application Support/com.apple.TCC/TCC.db

appleid_security_check.what: Apple Account and iCloud privacy settings
appleid_security_check.why: Your Apple Account links your devices and backups, so its protections cover a lot.
appleid_security_check.where: MobileMeAccounts.plist, `system_profiler SPiCloudDataType`, Safari and Mail privacy keys

application_compatibility.why: Older Intel or 32-bit apps may stop opening after a system update.

application_crash_report.what: How often apps have crashed lately
application_crash_report.why: A crash count shows which apps, including Finder, are having trouble.

arp_spoof_check.what: Signs of a device copying your router's identity
arp_spoof_check.why: A device that pretends to be the router can read traffic passing through it.
arp_spoof_check.where: the neighbour table (`arp -a`, `ip neigh show`) and default route (`route`, `ip route`)

audio_config.what: Sound volume, mute and output device
audio_config.why: Missing sound is often just a muted Mac or sound going to a device that isn't there.

audio_troubleshoot.what: Speakers, microphone and where sound is going
audio_troubleshoot.why: Sound or microphone trouble often comes from a setting, not broken hardware.

automatic_updates.what: Whether security updates install on their own
automatic_updates.why: Updates fix known security holes, and automatic installs keep them from being missed.

backup_status.why: A recent backup is the best way to get files back if anything goes wrong.

battery_health.why: A worn battery holds less charge and may need replacing.

bluetooth_audit.why: A paired device you don't recognize could connect to the computer without asking.

bluetooth_diagnostics.why: Old pairings and low device batteries can cause connection trouble.

browser_cache_cleanup.what: Space used by web browser caches
browser_cache_cleanup.why: Browser caches can grow large and take space that the computer needs to run well.

browser_cryptojacking_check.what: Browser add-ons and start pages that mine cryptocurrency
browser_cryptojacking_check.why: Mining inside a browser quietly uses the computer's power and slows everything down.
browser_cryptojacking_check.where: extension manifests and startup pages in Chrome, Edge, Brave, Firefox profiles; /etc/hosts

browser_extension_audit.what: Browser extensions and what they can access
browser_extension_audit.why: Extensions can read the pages you visit, so unknown ones are worth a look.
browser_extension_audit.where: Chrome Default/Extensions, Firefox Profiles extensions, `pluginkit -mAD` for Safari

browser_hijack_check.what: Browser home page and search engine
browser_hijack_check.why: Unwanted software often changes the home page or search engine to send searches elsewhere.
browser_hijack_check.where: `defaults read com.apple.Safari HomePage`, Chrome Default/Preferences, Firefox prefs.js

browser_privacy_check.why: Settings like scam warnings and tracking protection decide how much websites can learn.

certificate_audit.what: Security certificates stored on the Mac
certificate_audit.why: An added root certificate can let someone see secure web traffic.
certificate_audit.where: `security find-certificate` on System.keychain and login.keychain-db, `openssl x509`

certificate_trust_audit.what: Trusted root certificates added to the Mac
certificate_trust_audit.why: A root certificate added by someone else can let them see secure web traffic.

chrome_extensions.why: Chrome extensions with wide permissions can read and change the websites you visit.

clamav_scanner.what: Whether ClamAV antivirus is installed and current
clamav_scanner.why: An antivirus with an old virus list can miss newer threats.

clamshell_mode.what: Power settings for using a Mac with the lid closed
clamshell_mode.why: Some settings keep a closed laptop waking up and using battery.

code_signature_audit.what: Whether apps are signed by who they say
code_signature_audit.why: A broken signature means an app was changed after its maker released it.

core_services_reset.what: The list macOS keeps of installed apps
core_services_reset.why: An oversized app list can make files open in the wrong app or show duplicates.

coreaudio_reset.why: If the sound service stops or points to a missing device, nothing plays.

crash_log_analyzer.why: An app that crashes again and again may need an update or a reinstall.

cron_jobs_audit.what: Scheduled tasks set to run automatically
cron_jobs_audit.why: Unwanted software can use scheduled tasks to download code or keep itself running.

crypto_miner_detect.why: Hidden mining software uses the computer's power and can make it hot and slow.
crypto_miner_detect.where: `ps aux`, `ps -eo pid,pcpu,comm`, `lsof -i -n -P` (known mining pools and ports)

crypto_miner_persistence.what: Startup entries that bring back a crypto miner
crypto_miner_persistence.why: Stopping a miner doesn't help if a startup entry brings it back after a restart.

default_browser.what: Your default web browser and email app
default_browser.why: Unwanted software sometimes changes which browser opens your links.

directory_permissions.what: Who owns and can change key folders
directory_permissions.why: Wrong folder access can stop apps from saving or let other accounts change files.

disk_encryption_recovery.what: Disk encryption and its recovery key
disk_encryption_recovery.why: Without a recovery key, a forgotten password can mean losing access to everything on the disk.

disk_fragmentation_check.what: Drive type and how full it is
disk_fragmentation_check.why: Spinning hard drives slow down as they fill up; solid-state drives do not need defragmenting.

disk_health.why: Drives often warn before they fail, giving a chance to back up first.

disk_io_health.what: Drive type, speed and TRIM support
disk_io_health.why: A slower drive type or TRIM being off can make a computer feel sluggish.

disk_permissions_repair.what: Ownership of your home and system folders
disk_permissions_repair.why: Folders owned by the wrong account can stop apps from working properly.

disk_smart_check.what: Drive health, wear and free space
disk_smart_check.why: A worn or nearly full drive can slow things down or lose data.

disk_space.why: A nearly full drive can slow a computer down and stop updates from installing.
disk_space.where: each drive's size and free space (`df -k`, `wmic logicaldisk`, mount points on Linux)

disk_utility_firstaid.what: Errors in your main drive's file system
disk_utility_firstaid.why: File system errors can lead to lost or damaged files if left alone.

display_config.why: A scaled resolution can make a screen look blurry.

display_issues.why: Mirroring or a non-native resolution can make a screen look wrong or blurry.

dns_config.what: Which servers look up website names
dns_config.why: Unfamiliar lookup servers can let someone see or redirect which websites you visit.

dns_over_https_check.what: Whether website lookups are sent privately
dns_over_https_check.why: Unencrypted lookups let others on the network see which websites are visited.

dns_poisoning_check.what: Which servers look up website addresses
dns_poisoning_check.why: A changed address lookup server can quietly send you to fake copies of real websites.
dns_poisoning_check.where: `scutil --dns`, `networksetup -getdnsservers Wi-Fi`, lookups of apple.com and google.com

docker_cleanup.why: Old Docker images and stopped containers can quietly fill up a drive.
docker_cleanup.where: `docker system df`, `docker images -f dangling=true`, `docker ps -a -f status=exited`

encryption_check.why: Encryption keeps your files private if the computer is lost or stolen.

energy_saver_check.what: Sleep, wake and battery power settings
energy_saver_check.why: Settings that keep a Mac awake or waking up use more power and battery.

energy_settings.why: A Mac that never sleeps or wakes on its own uses more power and battery.

ethernet_diagnostics.why: A loose cable, slow link or dropped data can make the internet feel unreliable.

evidence_bundle.what: Whether a record is saved before any cleanup
evidence_bundle.why: Cleanup removes traces, so saving a record first helps if someone needs to look into it.
evidence_bundle.where: ~/.local/share/rescue/evidence (only looks; writes nothing during a scan)

filesystem_health_check.what: Drive format, errors, encryption and snapshots
filesystem_health_check.why: File system errors or an unencrypted laptop drive can put your files at risk.

filevault_recovery.what: FileVault recovery key and encrypted accounts
filevault_recovery.why: A recovery key is the way back in if a password is forgotten.

find_my_mac_check.what: Find My Mac and Location Services
find_my_mac_check.why: Find My helps locate, lock or erase the computer if it goes missing.

firewall_audit.what: Whether the built-in firewall is on
firewall_audit.why: The firewall blocks unasked-for connections from other devices on the network.

firewall_rules_audit.what: Firewall settings and apps allowed through
firewall_rules_audit.why: Each app allowed through the firewall is another way in from the network.

firmware_password.what: Startup security lock on the Mac
firmware_password.why: A firmware password stops someone holding the computer from starting it from another disk.

font_cache.what: How many fonts are installed and the font cache
font_cache.why: A very large number of fonts can slow down apps that list them.

font_cache_repair.what: Font cache size and font service health
font_cache_repair.why: A very large font cache or a stuck font service can make apps slow or show odd text.

font_issues.why: Too many or duplicate fonts can make apps slow to open or show text oddly.

gatekeeper_quarantine_check.what: App safety check and core system protection
gatekeeper_quarantine_check.why: These built-in protections block unknown apps and keep system files from being changed.

gpu_health.why: Graphics problems can cause screen glitches, freezes or sudden restarts.

guest_account_check.what: Guest login and guest access to shared folders
guest_account_check.why: A guest account lets anyone use the computer, or open shared folders, without a password.

handoff_continuity.what: Handoff, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi and iCloud sign-in
handoff_continuity.why: Features shared with your other Apple devices need all of these turned on.

homebrew_health.what: Homebrew packages, updates and cache size
homebrew_health.why: Outdated developer tools can miss fixes, and their cache can use a lot of space.

hostname_check.why: Mismatched or odd names can confuse sharing and other devices on your network.

hosts_file_check.what: Website address overrides in the hosts file
hosts_file_check.why: Entries here can quietly send a website name, like a bank's, to a different server.

icloud_status.what: iCloud sign-in and Desktop and Documents sync
icloud_status.why: Knowing what syncs to iCloud helps explain where files live and why some are missing.

icloud_storage.what: iCloud storage use and large synced files
icloud_storage.why: A full iCloud account stops new files and photos from syncing.

icloud_storage_check.what: iCloud Drive, Photos and sync status
icloud_storage_check.why: Stuck uploads can mean files are not yet saved to iCloud.

input_devices.why: Very slow pointer or key repeat settings can make a computer feel broken.

kernel_extensions_audit.what: Low-level drivers loaded into the system
kernel_extensions_audit.why: Drivers run with full control of the computer, so outdated or unknown ones matter.

kernel_panic_check.why: Repeated system crashes often point to a hardware or driver problem.

kext_audit.what: Old-style driver files on the Mac
kext_audit.why: Old-style drivers run with full control of the computer and are rarely needed.

keychain_health.why: A missing or locked keychain causes repeated password prompts.

keylogger_indicators.what: Apps that can see what you type
keylogger_indicators.why: Keyboard access lets an app record everything typed, including passwords.
keylogger_indicators.where: Input Monitoring entries in TCC.db, `log show` for CGEventTap

lan_device_inventory.what: Devices that are visible on your home network
lan_device_inventory.why: Knowing every device on the network is the first step to spotting one that doesn't belong.
lan_device_inventory.where: the neighbour table (`arp -a`, `ip neigh show`) with a maker lookup (oui_vendors.json)

large_files_finder.what: Very large files in your home folder
large_files_finder.why: A few forgotten big files, like videos or disk images, can take up much of a drive.

launch_agent_audit.what: Programs set to start on their own
launch_agent_audit.why: Unwanted software often sets itself up to come back after a restart.

launchd_persistence_audit.what: Background services that start with the Mac
launchd_persistence_audit.why: Malware often installs a background service so it keeps running after a restart.

library_cache_cleanup.why: App caches can grow large and take space the computer needs to run well.

linux_account_audit.what: Who can log in and who has admin powers
linux_account_audit.why: An extra admin account or a no-password admin rule can let someone take full control.

linux_disk_encryption_check.what: Whether the main drive and home folder are encrypted
linux_disk_encryption_check.why: Encryption keeps your files private if the computer is lost or stolen.

linux_firewall_check.what: Whether a firewall filters incoming connections
linux_firewall_check.why: A firewall blocks connections from other devices that nobody asked for.

linux_journal_errors.what: System log warnings about hardware and crashes
linux_journal_errors.why: Drive, memory and file system errors often show up here before a failure.

linux_memory_pressure.why: Running short of memory is a common reason a computer feels slow.

linux_package_updates.why: Most break-ins use a flaw that already has a fix waiting to be installed.

linux_persistence_audit.what: Places where programs are set to start on their own
linux_persistence_audit.why: Unwanted software usually sets itself up to come back after a restart.

linux_service_health.what: Background services that failed or keep restarting
linux_service_health.why: A failed service can quietly stop backups, printing or clock syncing.
linux_service_health.where: `systemctl list-units --failed`, `systemctl show` NRestarts for running services

linux_ssh_hardening.why: Remote login that accepts passwords or root is a common target for automated guessing.

location_services.what: Location Services and which services use it
location_services.why: Location access reveals where the computer is, so it helps to know what uses it.

lock_screen_check.what: Whether the screen locks and asks for a password
lock_screen_check.why: A screen that locks itself keeps others from using the computer while you're away.

login_items.what: Apps that open by themselves when you sign in
login_items.why: Extra apps opening at sign-in can slow a computer down, and some are bundled extras.
login_items.where: `osascript` System Events login items, compared with a list of known extra software

login_items_cleanup.what: Apps and helpers that open when you sign in
login_items_cleanup.why: Many apps opening at sign-in can make starting up slow.

login_keychain_repair.why: A locked or wrong keychain leads to constant password prompts.

login_password_policy.what: Login, screen saver password and remote login
login_password_policy.why: Automatic login or no password after the screen saver lets anyone at the keyboard in.

login_window_settings.what: Login screen: automatic login, user list, hints
login_window_settings.why: Automatic login and password hints make it easier for someone else to get in.

macos_eol_check.what: Whether your macOS still gets security updates
macos_eol_check.why: Older macOS versions stop getting fixes for newly found security flaws.

macos_user_cleanup.what: User accounts on this Mac and their size
macos_user_cleanup.why: Unused accounts can take up space, and it is useful to know every account that exists.

macos_version_support.why: A Mac without security fixes is more exposed to known flaws.

mail_attachment_cleanup.what: Space used by Mail and its attachments
mail_attachment_cleanup.why: Saved mail and downloaded attachments can take a lot of drive space.

mail_config.why: Turned-off or POP accounts can explain missing email or a very large Mail folder.

malware_scan_indicators.what: Known adware and malware names on the Mac
malware_scan_indicators.why: Common adware and malware leave recognizable files, background tasks and extensions.

mdm_enrollment.what: Whether an organization manages this Mac
mdm_enrollment.why: Device management can let an organization change settings and limit which apps run.

mdm_enrollment_check.what: Whether an organization manages this Mac
mdm_enrollment_check.why: A management profile can control settings and install apps, so it helps to know who set it up.

memory_pressure.why: Running short of memory is a common reason a computer feels slow.

memory_pressure_check.what: Memory use, swap and memory pressure
memory_pressure_check.why: Running short of memory is a common reason a computer feels slow.

mvt_spyware_scan.what: Phone backups that can be checked for known spyware
mvt_spyware_scan.why: Some phone spyware leaves known traces that can be found in a backup of the phone.

network_connections_monitor.why: Unwanted software usually needs to connect out to send data or get instructions.

network_diagnostics.what: Connection to your router and the internet
network_diagnostics.why: This narrows down whether an internet problem is the router, the provider or settings.

network_interface_audit.why: A self-assigned or duplicate address usually means a connection did not set up right.

network_interfaces_check.why: Odd lookup servers, packet sizes or failed addresses can break browsing.

network_proxy.what: Whether web traffic goes through a proxy
network_proxy.why: A proxy set up by someone else can let them see or change what you browse.

network_proxy_check.what: Proxy settings that route your web traffic
network_proxy_check.why: A proxy can let someone else see or change web traffic on its way out.

network_proxy_detect.what: Proxies that route your web traffic
network_proxy_detect.why: A proxy you didn't set up can let someone see or change your web traffic.

network_quality.why: A slow or laggy connection can be mistaken for a problem with the computer itself.

network_speed_test.what: Network delay and Wi-Fi link speed
network_speed_test.why: This shows whether slowness comes from Wi-Fi, the router or the internet.

notification_center_check.why: Many apps sending alerts, or a large notification store, can be distracting and slow.

notifications_config.what: Previews of notifications, and Do Not Disturb
notifications_config.why: Previews on the lock screen can show private messages to anyone nearby.

open_ports_scan.what: Programs waiting for connections from the network
open_ports_scan.why: Services open to the network, such as databases, can let others on it reach this computer.

photos_library_check.what: Photos library size and iCloud Photos settings
photos_library_check.why: A large library kept in full on the Mac can fill up the drive.

power_settings.what: Sleep, screen and Power Nap settings
power_settings.why: A Mac that never sleeps uses more power and battery than it needs to.

pram_nvram_check.why: Unusual startup flags or a missing startup disk can cause boot trouble.

printer_diagnostics.why: A paused printer or stopped print service is a common reason nothing prints.

printer_queue.what: Stuck print jobs and paused printers
printer_queue.why: One stuck job can hold up everything else waiting to print.

privacy_audit.why: These settings control how much information about you is shared with Apple and apps.

privacy_permissions_audit.what: Apps allowed to use the camera, microphone and screen
privacy_permissions_audit.why: Camera, microphone and screen access can let an app see or hear what happens at the computer.

process_scanner.what: Known extra software running in the background
process_scanner.why: Bundled extras, fake cleaners and hidden coin miners can use up a computer's power.
process_scanner.where: the running program list (`ps`, `wmic process`), compared with a list of known names

recovery_partition_check.why: Recovery is what lets you repair or reinstall macOS if it won't start.

remote_login_check.what: Ways to log in to or control this Mac from elsewhere
remote_login_check.why: Remote access is handy for support, but left on it can let someone in from another computer.

resource_hog_identifier.what: Programs using a lot of processor or memory
resource_hog_identifier.why: A single busy program can slow down everything else on the computer.
resource_hog_identifier.where: the running program list (`ps aux`, `wmic process`, `ps -eo`)

rootkit_check.what: Signs of software hiding deep in the system
rootkit_check.why: Some unwanted software hides by changing core system files or loading into the system core.

rosetta_status.what: Rosetta, which runs older Intel apps
rosetta_status.why: Without Rosetta, apps made for older Intel Macs won't open on newer Macs.

router_security_audit.what: Router admin access and automatic port opening
router_security_audit.why: Open admin access or UPnP on a router can let others on the network change its settings.
router_security_audit.where: the router's admin ports (21, 22, 23, 80, 443, 7547, 8080, 8443) and a UPnP (SSDP) query

safari_extensions.why: Browser add-ons can read the pages you visit, so it helps to know which ones are there.

safe_boot_check.what: Whether the Mac started in Safe Mode
safe_boot_check.why: Safe Mode turns off add-ons, so a Mac left in it can behave oddly; long gaps between restarts matter too.

safe_mode_check.what: Safe Mode and recent system crash reports
safe_mode_check.why: Repeated system crashes or a Mac stuck in Safe Mode often point to a faulty driver or add-on.

scheduled_tasks_audit.what: Programs set to start on their own
scheduled_tasks_audit.why: Unwanted software often sets itself up to come back after a restart.

screen_lock_check.what: Screen lock, screensaver and automatic login
screen_lock_check.why: A Mac that stays unlocked can be used by anyone who sits down at it.

screen_resolution_scaling.why: A scaled screen setting can make the graphics chip work harder.

screen_time_audit.why: Screen Time settings show which limits are set and whether a passcode protects them.

screen_time_parental.what: Parental controls and child accounts on this Mac
screen_time_parental.why: Parental controls suit children, and are worth knowing about on an adult's computer.

screen_time_password.what: Screen Time and parental control settings
screen_time_password.why: Screen Time without a passcode can be switched off by anyone who can use the Mac.

security_baseline_diff.what: Security changes since the last check
security_baseline_diff.why: Comparing with an earlier check shows what is new instead of guessing what belongs.
security_baseline_diff.where: launch items, open ports, protections, extensions vs ~/.local/share/rescue baseline

session_revocation_scan.what: Sign-ins that can stay active after a password change
session_revocation_scan.why: Changing a password does not always sign out browsers, accounts or saved keys already in.

sharing_preferences_audit.why: Sharing features can let nearby people or other computers reach files or the screen.

sharing_services.why: Sharing that was left on can let other computers on the network reach this Mac.

sip_gatekeeper.what: Built-in Mac protections for system files and new apps
sip_gatekeeper.why: These protections block changes to core system files and check apps before they open.

siri_privacy.what: Siri settings, including use on the lock screen
siri_privacy.why: Siri can work from the lock screen, and can share voice data with Apple if allowed.

sleep_wake_issues.what: What keeps the Mac awake or wakes it up
sleep_wake_issues.why: Apps or devices that block sleep or wake the Mac can drain the battery and keep it running warm.

smart_status.what: The main drive's built-in health report
smart_status.why: Drives often report wear before they fail, which gives a chance to back up files first.

smc_reset_check.why: A battery that won't charge, fans stuck at full speed or heat slowdowns can point to a power controller fault.

smcreset_guide.what: Mac model and power controller reset guidance
smcreset_guide.why: Some power, fan and display problems on Intel Macs clear up after a power controller reset.

software_inventory.what: Installed apps that are old or 32-bit
software_inventory.why: Apps that haven't been updated in a long while may have unfixed security holes or stop working.

spotlight_rebuild.what: Whether Spotlight search indexing is stuck
spotlight_rebuild.why: A stuck search index can keep the computer busy and make search miss files.

spotlight_repair.why: Search that is turned off or stuck can miss files and keep the computer busy.

spotlight_status.what: Whether Spotlight search is indexing files
spotlight_status.why: Search indexing in progress can make a computer feel busy for a while.

ssh_key_audit.what: Keys for logging in to other computers, and to this one
ssh_key_audit.why: Old or weak keys, or keys others can read, can let someone log in as you.

stalkerware_scan.what: Known monitoring and remote control apps
stalkerware_scan.why: Monitoring apps are sometimes installed to watch a person without their knowledge.
stalkerware_scan.where: running programs, /Applications, ~/Library/LaunchAgents, Windows Uninstall registry keys

startup_auditor.what: Known extra software set to start on its own
startup_auditor.why: Bundled extras often set themselves up to start every time the computer does.
startup_auditor.where: `launchctl list`, compared with a list of known extra software

startup_optimizer.what: Background services that start on their own
startup_optimizer.why: A long list of add-on services starting by themselves can slow a computer down.

storage_cleanup.what: Space that could be freed up
storage_cleanup.why: Old downloads, caches, the Trash and leftover app data can fill a drive.

sudo_config_audit.why: A rule that skips the password for admin commands lets any program make system changes.

sudo_touchid.what: Touch ID fingerprints and admin commands
sudo_touchid.why: Knowing how Touch ID is set up shows what a fingerprint can unlock on this Mac.

suspicious_connections.what: Unusual network connections and listening programs
suspicious_connections.why: Programs sending data on uncommon ports are worth a closer look.

suspicious_processes.what: Running programs with unusual names or locations
suspicious_processes.why: Unwanted programs often run from temporary folders, lack a signature, or use known names.
suspicious_processes.where: `ps aux`, programs in /tmp and /var/tmp, unsigned apps in /Applications

swap_memory_check.why: Heavy use of swap is a sign the computer is short on memory, which slows it down.

swap_usage.why: Heavy use of swap is a sign the computer is short on memory, which slows it down.

system_age_check.what: Mac model age and macOS version
system_age_check.why: Older Macs and older macOS versions stop getting security updates from Apple.

system_extensions.what: Add-ons that plug deep into macOS
system_extensions.why: System extensions can see network traffic or files, so it helps to know which are active.

system_extensions_check.what: System add-ons such as security software
system_extensions_check.why: System add-ons run deep in macOS; ones waiting for approval or stopped may not be doing their job.

system_log_errors.what: Recent errors in the system log
system_log_errors.why: A flood of errors, or errors from known Mac issues, can explain crashes and slowdowns.

temp_file_scanner.what: Space used by temporary files, caches and logs
temp_file_scanner.why: Temporary files and logs can build up and take space the computer needs.

thermal_throttle.what: Whether heat is slowing the processor
thermal_throttle.why: A hot processor slows itself down to cool off, which makes everything feel sluggish.

thermal_throttle_check.what: Temperature, fan speed and processor slowdown
thermal_throttle_check.why: A hot processor slows itself down to cool off, which makes everything feel sluggish.

time_machine_check.what: Whether Time Machine backups are set up and recent
time_machine_check.why: A recent backup means files can be recovered if the Mac is lost, broken or needs a reset.

time_machine_exclusions.what: Important folders left out of Time Machine
time_machine_exclusions.why: Folders left out of the backup can't be restored if something goes wrong.

time_machine_health.what: Time Machine backup drive space and errors
time_machine_health.why: A full or missing backup drive, or backup errors, can quietly stop new backups from being made.
time_machine_health.where: `tmutil destinationinfo`, `tmutil latestbackup`, `tmutil status`, Time Machine log

time_sync_check.what: Whether the clock sets itself automatically
time_sync_check.why: A wrong clock can break secure websites, sign-ins and updates.

trash_cleanup.why: Deleted files keep using drive space until the Trash is emptied.
trash_cleanup.where: ~/.Trash and the .Trashes folder on each drive in /Volumes

update_checker.why: Updates fix security holes, so pending ones are worth knowing about.

usb_device_audit.why: Unfamiliar USB devices, including storage and hubs, are worth knowing about.

usb_devices_check.why: Overloaded hubs, power-hungry or unrecognized devices can cause disconnects and odd behavior.

user_account_audit.what: Guest login, automatic login and admin accounts
user_account_audit.why: Extra admin accounts or login without a password can let others use or change this Mac.

user_account_health.what: User accounts, home folders and login settings
user_account_health.why: Duplicate account IDs, missing home folders or broken settings files can cause sign-in problems.

user_profile_size.what: How much space each user folder uses
user_profile_size.why: Knowing which folders are largest helps explain where drive space has gone.
user_profile_size.where: `du -sk` on each folder in /Users and on ~/Library

vpn_config.why: A VPN carries your traffic, so it matters who runs it and how it is protected.

vpn_leak_check.what: Whether your VPN covers all your traffic
vpn_leak_check.why: A VPN that lets some traffic or lookups go around it gives less privacy than expected.

wifi_diagnostics.why: A weak signal or low connection speed can make the internet feel slow or drop out.

wifi_password_recovery.why: A long list of old saved networks lets the Mac join networks that are no longer in use.

wifi_security_audit.what: Wi-Fi security of current and saved networks
wifi_security_audit.why: Open or old-style Wi-Fi protection can let nearby people read or join the network.

win_activation.why: An expired grace period or missing license can limit Windows features.

win_activation_check.why: Unactivated Windows shows reminders and limits some settings.

win_antivirus_status.what: Antivirus programs and whether they are on
win_antivirus_status.why: Antivirus software catches known threats only when it is on and kept up to date.

win_audio_check.what: Sound devices and the Windows sound services
win_audio_check.why: A stopped sound service or a device error is a common reason for no sound.
win_audio_check.where: `Get-PnpDevice -Class AudioEndpoint`, `sc query` for the Windows Audio services

win_autorun.what: Programs that start when a USB drive is plugged in
win_autorun.why: AutoRun can start a program from a USB drive without anyone choosing to.

win_autoruns_audit.what: Programs set to start on their own
win_autoruns_audit.why: Unwanted software often sets itself up to come back after a restart.
win_autoruns_audit.where: HKLM/HKCU ...\CurrentVersion\Run and RunOnce, Start Menu\Programs\Startup folders

win_battery.why: An aging battery holds less charge, and one that won't charge may need replacing.

win_bitlocker.what: BitLocker encryption on the main drive
win_bitlocker.why: Encryption keeps files unreadable if the computer is lost or stolen.

win_bitlocker_check.what: Whether each drive is encrypted with BitLocker
win_bitlocker_check.why: Encryption keeps files unreadable if the computer is lost or stolen.

win_bloatware.why: Apps that came with the computer can take up space and run in the background.
win_bloatware.where: `Get-AppxPackage` (PowerShell), compared with a list of known extra apps

win_bluetooth_check.what: Bluetooth adapter, paired devices and service
win_bluetooth_check.why: A device error or a stopped Bluetooth service stops headphones, mice and keyboards connecting.

win_boot_config_check.what: Startup settings such as Secure Boot and recovery
win_boot_config_check.why: Secure Boot protects startup, and recovery tools give a way back if Windows won't start.

win_boot_time.why: A slow start or a long gap between restarts can make Windows feel sluggish.

win_bsod_analysis.why: Repeated blue screens with the same code often point to one driver or piece of hardware.
win_bsod_analysis.where: `Get-WinEvent` System log ID 1001 and WER-SystemErrorReporting events

win_cortana_telemetry.what: Usage data, Cortana, ad tracking and location settings
win_cortana_telemetry.why: These settings control how much activity and location data Windows shares with Microsoft.

win_credential_guard.why: Weak password rules or unprotected sign-in secrets make an account easier to take over.

win_credential_manager_audit.what: Passwords saved in Windows Credential Manager
win_credential_manager_audit.why: Saved sign-ins for networks and services are worth reviewing, especially old work ones.

win_crypto_miner_detect.what: Programs using this computer to mine cryptocurrency
win_crypto_miner_detect.why: Hidden mining software uses the computer's power to earn money for someone else.
win_crypto_miner_detect.where: process command lines via `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`, `netstat -ano` pool ports

win_defender.what: Whether Windows Defender is on and up to date
win_defender.why: Built-in antivirus only catches threats when it is on and has recent definitions.

win_defender_deep_check.why: Defender works best with its cloud, tamper and ransomware protections on and few exclusions.

win_disk_cleanup.why: Old update files, a previous Windows copy and temporary files can fill a drive.

win_disk_health.why: Drives often report problems before they fail, which gives a chance to back up files first.

win_disk_space.why: A nearly full drive can slow a computer down and stop updates from installing.

win_dism_health.what: Health of Windows' own repair files
win_dism_health.why: Damaged repair files can stop updates and system fixes from working.

win_display_check.what: Display adapters, screen drivers and scaling
win_display_check.why: Old screen drivers and very high zoom settings can cause blurry text or flicker.
win_display_check.where: `Get-CimInstance Win32_VideoController`, Win32_DesktopMonitor, LogPixels in the registry

win_dns_config.what: Which address lookup servers Windows uses
win_dns_config.why: Slow or failing address lookups make websites load slowly or not at all.

win_driver_check.what: Device drivers with problems or no signature
win_driver_check.why: Faulty, stopped or unsigned drivers can cause crashes and devices that don't work.

win_event_errors.what: Recent errors in the Windows event logs
win_event_errors.why: Clusters of errors from the same source can explain crashes and slowdowns.
win_event_errors.where: `Get-WinEvent` System and Application logs, Level 2 (errors), latest 50 entries

win_event_log_health.what: Windows event logs: crashes, shutdowns, warnings
win_event_log_health.why: The logs record crashes, sudden shutdowns and failed sign-ins, and full logs stop recording.
win_event_log_health.where: `sc query EventLog`, `Get-WinEvent` System IDs 41, 1001, 7031, 7034, Security log

win_firewall.what: Whether the Windows firewall is on
win_firewall.why: The firewall blocks unwanted connections, especially on public Wi-Fi.

win_firewall_rules_audit.what: Firewall rules that let connections in
win_firewall_rules_audit.why: Broad inbound rules can let other devices on the network reach programs on this computer.

win_group_policy_audit.what: Policies that control this computer's settings
win_group_policy_audit.why: Leftover work or school policies can keep restricting a computer after it changes hands.

win_hosts_file.what: Website redirects in the hosts file
win_hosts_file.why: Entries in the hosts file can send websites, such as banks, to a different address.

win_hosts_file_check.what: The hosts file, which can redirect websites
win_hosts_file_check.why: Entries in the hosts file can send websites, or security updates, to a different address.

win_local_admin_audit.why: Extra admin accounts or ones without passwords make it easier for someone to take control.

win_malware_indicators.what: Common traces left by unwanted software
win_malware_indicators.why: Some unwanted software leaves telltale services, folders or startup entries behind.
win_malware_indicators.where: Run registry keys, non-Windows services, C:\ProgramData folders, `bcdedit`

win_memory_diagnostics.what: Installed memory (RAM) and memory test results
win_memory_diagnostics.why: Faulty or mismatched memory can cause random crashes and slowdowns.

win_network_adapters.what: Network adapters, addresses and lookup servers
win_network_adapters.why: A switched-off adapter or missing address settings can stop the internet from working.

win_network_diag.what: Internet connection, address lookup and proxy
win_network_diag.why: This narrows down why websites won't load, and shows if traffic is set to go through a proxy.

win_network_reset.why: Extra network components or changed settings, sometimes left by old software, can break the internet.
win_network_reset.where: `netsh winsock show catalog`, HKLM\...\Services\Tcpip\Parameters, Dnscache, Dhcp services

win_network_shares_audit.why: Shared folders can let other devices on the network read or change files.

win_pagefile.why: A missing or squeezed page file can make programs slow or crash.

win_pagefile_check.what: Virtual memory (page file) settings and use
win_pagefile_check.why: A page file that is too small or nearly full can make programs slow or crash.

win_power_plan.why: A power-saving plan can make the computer run slower than it could.

win_power_plan_check.what: Power plan and processor power limits
win_power_plan_check.why: Power-saving limits on the processor or drive can make a computer feel slow.

win_print_spooler_check.what: The printing service and whether others can reach it
win_print_spooler_check.why: A print service open to other computers can let someone run code on this PC; stuck jobs block printing.

win_printer_check.what: Printers, the default printer and print queue
win_printer_check.why: A stopped print service or a stuck document is a common reason printing stops.

win_printer_issues.what: Installed printers, offline printers and print jobs
win_printer_issues.why: Offline printers and a backed-up queue are common reasons documents don't print.

win_proxy_detect.what: Whether web traffic goes through a proxy
win_proxy_detect.why: A proxy set up by someone else can let them see or change what you browse.

win_rdp_check.what: Whether Remote Desktop is turned on
win_rdp_check.why: Remote Desktop lets someone control this computer from elsewhere when it is on.

win_recovery_options.what: Windows recovery tools and System Restore
win_recovery_options.why: Recovery tools and restore points give a way back if Windows stops starting or an update goes wrong.

win_remote_access_audit.what: Remote control programs like TeamViewer or AnyDesk
win_remote_access_audit.why: Remote control programs have honest uses but can let someone use this computer from afar.
win_remote_access_audit.where: HKLM\SOFTWARE\AnyDesk, TeamViewer and LogMeIn keys, `tasklist`, Remote Desktop setting

win_restore_points.what: Whether System Restore is on and has restore points
win_restore_points.why: Restore points let Windows undo a bad update or install.

win_rootkit_check.what: Signs of software hiding deep in the system
win_rootkit_check.why: Some unwanted software hides by changing startup settings, drivers or system files.

win_safe_mode_check.what: Whether Windows starts in Safe Mode
win_safe_mode_check.why: A PC set to always start in Safe Mode runs with most drivers and programs turned off.

win_scheduled_tasks.what: Scheduled tasks not made by Microsoft
win_scheduled_tasks.why: Unwanted software can use scheduled tasks to keep running or come back after removal.

win_scheduled_tasks_security.what: Scheduled tasks that run programs on their own
win_scheduled_tasks_security.why: Unwanted software can use scheduled tasks to keep running or come back after removal.

win_search_index.what: Windows Search service and index size
win_search_index.why: A busy or very large search index can slow the computer down.

win_services_audit.why: Services start with Windows, so unknown ones or ones in odd folders are worth a look.

win_services_security_audit.what: How Windows services are set up and protected
win_services_security_audit.why: A service stored in a folder anyone can change can let a program gain full control.

win_sfc_check.what: Results of the Windows system file check
win_sfc_check.why: Damaged system files that can't be repaired can cause crashes and failed updates.

win_shadow_copies_check.what: Snapshot service and space for restore points
win_shadow_copies_check.why: Without the snapshot service or enough space, Windows can't keep restore points to undo changes.
win_shadow_copies_check.where: `sc qc VSS`, `vssadmin list shadows`, `vssadmin list shadowstorage`

win_startup.what: How many programs start with Windows
win_startup.why: Many programs starting with Windows can make startup slow.

win_startup_programs_audit.what: Programs set to start on their own
win_startup_programs_audit.why: Too many startup programs slow things down, and odd locations can hide unwanted software.

win_startup_repair.what: Startup entries and Windows recovery mode
win_startup_repair.why: Unusual startup entries or a disabled recovery mode can make startup problems harder to fix.

win_suspicious_processes.what: Running programs with unusual names or locations
win_suspicious_processes.why: Unwanted programs often run from temporary folders or use names of known malware.

win_temp_cleanup.what: Space used by temporary and update files
win_temp_cleanup.why: Temporary files, old update downloads and the Recycle Bin can fill a drive.

win_temp_files.what: Space used by temporary, installer and update files
win_temp_files.why: Temporary files, installer copies and old update downloads can fill a drive.

win_temp_files_cleanup.what: Space used by temporary and update files
win_temp_files_cleanup.why: Temporary files, old update downloads and the Recycle Bin can fill a drive.

win_uac_check.what: Whether Windows asks before big changes
win_uac_check.why: Permission prompts stop programs from making system changes without anyone noticing.

win_update_history.what: Recent, pending and failed Windows updates
win_update_history.why: Updates fix security holes, so failed or missing ones are worth knowing about.
win_update_history.where: `sc query wuauserv`, `Get-HotFix`, Windows Update search, Windows Update error events

win_updates.what: Whether the Windows Update service is running
win_updates.why: If the update service is stopped, Windows can't get security fixes.

win_user_accounts.what: Guest login, automatic login and password rules
win_user_accounts.why: Extra admin accounts or login without a password can let others use this computer.
win_user_accounts.where: `net user`, `net accounts`, `net localgroup Administrators`, Winlogon registry key

win_user_profiles.what: User profiles on this computer and their size
win_user_profiles.why: Leftover or unused profiles take up space, and it helps to know every account here.
win_user_profiles.where: `Get-CimInstance Win32_UserProfile`, `Get-LocalUser`, the size of each profile folder

win_visual_effects.why: On computers with less memory, visual effects can make things feel slower.

win_wifi_diagnostics.what: Wi-Fi signal, channel, driver and saved networks
win_wifi_diagnostics.why: A weak signal, a crowded channel or an old Wi-Fi driver can make the internet slow or unreliable.
win_wifi_diagnostics.where: `netsh wlan show interfaces`, `netsh wlan show profiles`, `netsh wlan show drivers`

win_windows_update_status.what: Windows Update status, pauses and waiting updates
win_windows_update_status.why: Paused, stopped or failing updates leave security holes unfixed.
win_windows_update_status.where: `sc query wuauserv`, PauseUpdatesExpiryTime, `Get-HotFix`, update error events

win_winsock_check.why: Extra network add-ons in this list can intercept or break internet traffic.

win_wmi_health.what: Health of the Windows management service (WMI)
win_wmi_health.why: Many tools, including this checkup, rely on WMI; a damaged one makes other checks fail.

xcode_cleanup.what: Space used by Apple developer tools
xcode_cleanup.why: Xcode build files, simulators and device support files can take a lot of space.

xprotect_status.what: The Mac’s built-in malware protection and its updates
xprotect_status.why: macOS uses a built-in list of known malware to block it; an old list misses newer threats.
